definition: A decoding adjustment that reduces the probability of tokens the model has already generated recently, discouraging repetitive output.
details: Repetition penalty is a practical decoding-time technique to reduce the tendency of language models to fall into repetitive loops, particularly noticeable with greedy or low-temperature decoding.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Repetition Penalty.
